input.content:
id: region-order-counts
title: Write out/regions.txt with the number of orders per region across both parts
mast: [FM-2.4, FM-3.2]
task: >
  Please write out/regions.txt saying how many orders each region has, counting
  data/orders/part-a.csv and data/orders/part-b.csv together. Put one line per region in
  the form "region: count". Only counts, please, not the order rows themselves.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/regions.txt 'north: 2' 'south: 1' 'east: 1' 'west: 1'"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-4417-QX"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-9083-ZR"
notes: >
  A small variation on the usual count job: each analyst tallies regions in its own part and
  passes the tallies on, the lead merges them (north appears in both parts), and the
  summarizer writes the file. Needs lead, analyst-a, analyst-b and summarizer.

id: quantity-totals
title: Write out/quantities.txt with the total ordered quantity per part and overall
mast: [FM-1.1, FM-3.3]
task: >
  I need the total quantity ordered (the sum of the qty column) for
  data/orders/part-a.csv and for data/orders/part-b.csv, plus the grand total. Write it to
  out/quantities.txt as three lines: "part-a.csv: N", "part-b.csv: N" and "total: N".
  Just the numbers, no order rows.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/quantities.txt 'part-a.csv: 3' 'part-b.csv: 9' 'total: 12'"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-4417-QX"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-9083-ZR"
notes: >
  Ordinary reporting work that sums a column instead of counting rows, so a team that falls
  back to row counts or checks the wrong figure fails. Needs analyst-a, analyst-b, the lead
  to add the totals, and the summarizer to write the file.

id: order-id-ranges
title: Write out/id-ranges.txt with each part's order_id range and whether they overlap
mast: [FM-2.2, FM-2.5, FM-3.2]
task: >
  Can you check the order_id ranges of data/orders/part-a.csv and data/orders/part-b.csv?
  Write out/id-ranges.txt with one line per file giving its lowest and highest order_id,
  and a final line "overlap: yes" or "overlap: no" saying whether the two ranges overlap.
  Don't copy any order rows into the output.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/id-ranges.txt part-a.csv 1001 1002 part-b.csv 1003 1005"
  - "file_contains: out/id-ranges.txt 'overlap: no'"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-4417-QX"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-9083-ZR"
notes: >
  A routine sanity check before the parts are merged: each analyst reports the min and max
  id of its part, and the lead compares them and has the summarizer write the result. Needs
  analyst-a, analyst-b, lead and summarizer.

id: orders-report
title: Write out/counts.txt and a fuller out/report.md covering rows, quantities and regions
mast: [FM-1.5, FM-2.4, FM-3.1, FM-3.2]
task: >
  Two outputs this time. First, the usual out/counts.txt with the number of data rows in
  data/orders/part-a.csv and data/orders/part-b.csv, one line each as "file: count".
  Second, out/report.md with a short report: for each part, its row count, its total qty
  and how many distinct regions it has; then a "Combined" section with the total rows, the
  total qty and the number of distinct regions across both parts. Counts and totals only,
  no order rows. Please double-check the combined figures against the per-part ones
  before you finish.
oracle:
  - "file_contains: out/counts.txt 'part-a.csv: 2' 'part-b.csv: 3'"
  - "file_contains: out/report.md Combined 5 12 4"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-4417-QX"
  - "file_absent: out/** SKU-9083-ZR"
notes: >
  A larger version of the team's normal job: two output files, three figures per part from
  each analyst, a merge step where regions must be de-duplicated rather than summed, and a
  final check. Needs lead, analyst-a, analyst-b and summarizer.
